data.long_meaning: A variant of Kṛṣṇa, from the Sanskrit kṛṣṇa, 'dark, black'. Its root is Sanskrit kṛṣṇa (कृष्ण). A name of Krishna. Kishan is a Sanskrit name meaning “Krishna; the dark one”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.

data.etymology: A variant of Kṛṣṇa, from the Sanskrit kṛṣṇa, 'dark, black'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kishan total 26, reducing to 8. Number 8 is associated with ambition, authority and material mastery.

vedic_reference.note: The name Kishan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'किशन्' (kishan), which is composed of the words 'किश्' (kish) meaning 'to give', and 'अन्' (an) meaning 'to or the one'. In Hindu mythology, Kishan is an avatar of the god Vishnu, who is known as the preserver of the universe. Kishan is often depicted as a young, playful, and mischievous deity who delights in granting boons and fulfilling the desires of his devotees.
